expected.match_note: Ids, enums, numbers, dates and times are compared exactly. Free-text values (goal, why, success, notes, what) are compared by meaning, not wording. Objects inside lists are compared on the keys given. Fields not listed keep the defaults from assets/workspace/.

Learner notes: Prefers few questions: ask only when a decision needs it

readback_mentions: Rust, for fun; capstone: a CLI tool that parses a CSV, with tests
no date: 4-week cycles, each ending with a capstone check-in
whenever: no fixed sessions, no calendar
checks: Express path: at most 5 learner replies during onboarding.
Q3, Q4, Q5, Q7 and Q8 are not asked during onboarding; each is asked later on its own, only when it becomes needed, never as a batch.
Express starts from the first message: the opener echoes it, promises 3 questions and lists no others.

While 'prefers few questions' stands: the scope map is a statement, Q4 carries the theory-source question, Q5 asks only age and first language (tone stays B), and the 10-minute warning is a statement that defaults to closing.
No file exists in the workspace before the readback 'yes'.
The preview shows the next useful windows (for example, the 2-day recheck 44 to 72 hours after the first session), not fixed weekly slots.
The first measurement is a short capstone attempt in the editor (compiler allowed, no AI, no docs) plus a few concept probes.
On-demand: no attendance, missed-block or execution questions, even after 9 days away; the next open simply shows what is due.
No calendar event and no .ics file are created unless the learner asks.
Claude never writes the learner's solution code or edits the learner's exercise files.
Learner-facing text contains no E-, B-, S- or L- ids, no answers and no emojis.
